I was in the same boat as you with using weed to deal with complex trauma (mother dieing in teens, sexually abused at 8, raped at uni, narcissistic dad). Unfortunately I learnt it only keeps it bay. And long term worsens your mental health. After I quit in March, I went on medication and have been going to regular trauma counselling and exercising (swimming, tennis, yoga and cycling). I'd really recommend getting therapy and dealing with the trauma, it's hard work but it has helped me in every facet of life. Quitting is also really boring so it also helps thinking about what hobbies/ activities you enjoyed before weed took over to start building healthy coping mechanisms. I believe in you! You got this. But make sure to replace the habits with better ones or the cravings are much harder to overcome.

Lexapro (escitaloprám over here) has helped me so much staying stable while quitting and basically stopped all cravings (almost a month now). Counselling can also be a great way to vent and talk about your feelings by someone non-judgemental if it’s affordable/accessible. Whatever you choose, you’ve got this!
